reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer #1 characterized the work as a model-based evaluation of elevated-pressure PEC water splitting that analyzes benefits and penalties across bubble characteristics, crossover, optical loss, and concentration overpotential. The final paper states the same multiphysics scope and identifies a 6–8 bar range in P:S-7f2a1b1aea1e06422cc1.

Reviewer #3 questioned whether Pt-decorated FTO measurements at constant current adequately represent photoelectrochemical operation and noted that much of the analysis also applies to electrolysis. The final paper limits the calculation to a membrane-free configuration and states that photoelectrode surface properties and bubble nucleation/growth are not included in P:S-4fe694bd2d82eb3a81ee.

Reviewer #1 specifically recognized the integrated treatment of bubble characteristics, product crossover, bubble-induced optical losses, and concentration overpotential. The final paper describes a model that combines empirical bubble data, experimental observations, and these loss mechanisms in P:S-86266c1b2092069e85d0.

The reviewer requested clarification of the experimental basis for the fitting equations. The response explains that independent low-pressure experiments were used for validation, and the final paper reports comparison with lower-current-density literature data plus O2 bubble observations in P:S-da938de01210e29e3973.

Reviewer #1 identified electrode-adhered bubbles, shielding, and associated overpotential as not clearly included in the model. The final paper explicitly states that adhesion and the resulting overpotential are not directly simulated, relying instead on a gas-volume-fraction estimate and empirical correlation in P:S-3ade2f29fe8dc3b6c4bb.

Reviewer #1 questioned applicability from a membrane-free cell to the membrane/separator-based PEC reactors expected to scale. The final conclusion identifies its optimum only for membrane-free devices and confines the quantitative comparison to specified loss mechanisms in P:S-4fe694bd2d82eb3a81ee.

Reviewers questioned transfer from thin-film Pt/FTO to nanostructured photoelectrodes and the suitability of the surrogate setup for PEC-specific effects. The final paper confirms that morphology, wettability, electrolyte concentration, and bubble nucleation/growth can alter characteristics but are not represented in the Euler–Euler model in P:S-4fe694bd2d82eb3a81ee; the experimental electrode is Pt/FTO in P:S-8e18bf568c6f9149b5d9.

Reviewer #3 asked how optical loss and local pH were monitored. The response clarified that these are simulated quantities, and the final paper states that direct measurements of optical loss, crossover, and pH distribution are not yet technically feasible at elevated pressure in P:S-4fe694bd2d82eb3a81ee and P:S-ebc172c6cb3be824b498.

Reviewer #3 asked how experiments could extend above the stated 4-bar safe operating limit. The response distinguishes 1–4 bar validation experiments from simulations at 1–10 bar or higher; the final paper likewise describes experimental validation in a moderately pressurized cell and simulations up to 10 bar in P:S-ebc172c6cb3be824b498.

Reviewer #1 asked how broadly the conclusions apply across membrane choices and electrode surface properties. The final paper acknowledges unmodeled configuration-dependent factors, including mechanical strength, pumping loss, durability, surface properties, and bubble nucleation/growth, in P:S-4fe694bd2d82eb3a81ee.
Audit-only: the responses clarify that crossover, optical-loss, and local-pH results are simulated, and the final paper labels the multiphysics outputs as simulated in P:S-7bf9e3e8a0e1fe7a21cb.
Audit-only: the response supplies the imaging setup and explains electrode-specific focusing; the final methods record the Pt/FTO experiment and camera configuration in P:S-8e18bf568c6f9149b5d9.

Audit-only: the response distinguishes fitting data from independent validation data; the final paper reports the low-current-density comparison and experimental O2 bubble validation in P:S-da938de01210e29e3973.

limiting_points.suggested_action: State the scope of the pressure optimum in relation to unmodeled PEC-specific processes.
limiting_points.text: The elevated-pressure framing is limited by use of Pt/FTO surrogate electrodes and a model that does not represent several photoelectrode- and interface-specific processes.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain the explicit elevated-pressure PEC problem framing.
supporting_points.text: The contribution is a coupled assessment of elevated-pressure PEC water splitting that weighs pressure-dependent benefits and penalties across several device-loss mechanisms.

questions.suggested_action: Report the validation domain separately from the simulation domain and its uncertainty.
questions.text: What evidence constrains the predicted loss trade-offs and 6–8 bar operating range above the 1–4 bar experimental validation domain?

questions.suggested_action: Characterize sensitivity to device configuration and interface-dependent bubble behavior.
questions.text: How sensitive are the predicted pressure trends and optimum to membrane use, photoelectrode morphology and wettability, electrolyte composition, and unmodeled bubble nucleation and growth?

strengths.suggested_action: Preserve the integrated accounting of competing pressure-dependent loss mechanisms.
strengths.text: The analysis brings bubble characteristics, product crossover, optical scattering, concentration overpotential, thermodynamic voltage, and compression work into one pressure-dependent framework.

strengths.suggested_action: Keep the distinction between fitting data and independent validation data explicit.
strengths.text: The bubble-property model is checked against lower-current-density literature data and independent O2 bubble observations in a moderately pressurized cell.

summary.text: The review concerns a multiphysics assessment of elevated-pressure, membrane-free PEC water splitting that integrates pressure-dependent bubble behavior with crossover, optical, electrochemical, and compression losses. It recognizes the integrated framework and bubble-model checks, while retaining limits from indirect treatment of electrode bubble coverage, restricted transferability to practical PEC architectures and photoelectrodes, and unavailable direct validation of key loss mechanisms at elevated pressure.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantify the effect of direct bubble-coverage and shielding physics on the loss balance.
weaknesses.text: Bubble adherence, shielding, and the associated overpotential are not directly solved by the Euler–Euler model; they are estimated indirectly from gas volume fraction and an empirical correlation.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Bound conclusions to membrane-free devices or provide a configuration-specific comparison.
weaknesses.text: The reported optimum is derived for a membrane-free configuration, leaving its quantitative transfer to membrane/separator-based PEC reactors unresolved.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Assess how photoelectrode material and surface-dependent bubble behavior alter the modeled pressure response.
weaknesses.text: Using Pt/FTO surrogate electrodes does not establish how nanostructured photoelectrode morphology, wettability, and light-coupled operation affect bubble behavior and the PEC-specific loss balance.

weaknesses.suggested_action: State which central loss contributions remain simulation-only and their resulting uncertainty.
weaknesses.text: Optical loss, product crossover, and local pH/concentration-overpotential predictions remain simulation-based because direct elevated-pressure measurements were not yet technically feasible.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: Figure-result provenance was clarified as simulated; no retained point is assigned to this resolved clarity issue.
The imaging setup and electrode-specific focusing procedure were added; no retained point is assigned to this resolved methods clarification.
The final paper distinguishes correlation fitting from independent experimental checks; no retained point is assigned to this resolved data-inclusion clarification.
